Co-taught college success class for incoming Embry-Riddle College of Engineering freshmen in Fall 2024.
Assisted ERAU students with class registration.

positions.title: Material Management/Event Support
positions.description: Worked with a team of around 5 employees in managing event materials and setting up large venues for school events.

positions.title: System Engineering Intern
positions.description:
- Maintained and improved VHF and UHF radios for international defense use
- Performed radio tests while following over 600 pages of software verification testing documentation
- Created cross communication methods between a signal generator and a radio via NI VISA drivers
- Scripted automated calibration and test program in C# to save roughly 40 minutes per radio
- Developed and implemented functions to calibrate the radio’s watt meter and run power tests 
- Produced easy to operate graphical user interfaces (GUI) via Visual Studio and Windows Forms
- Collaborated with radio technicians to test, receive feedback on, and iterate program features
- Wrote around 2000 lines of code and documented program functionality in a 50 page manual

positions.title: Sales Warehouser I
positions.description:
- Efficiently picked and loaded chip boxes onto the correct trucks with over 99% efficiency
- Led new employees in breaking down empty chip boxes and building up pallets of flattened boxes
- Assisted fellow employees by picking product for their routes after finishing my appointed work 
- Recommended a new procedure to my manager which was implemented a few weeks later
- Received a Pepsi-co silver award for making a “great impact to the team”

projects.title: NASA Revolutionary Aerospace Systems Concepts Academic Linkage  (RASCAL)
projects.description:
Worked with a transdisciplinary group of 13 talented individuals and 2 faculty mentors from across multiple ERAU campuses including Daytona Beach, FL and worldwide on designing a multi-use platform to be stationed at the first Earth-Moon LaGrange point. 
- Documented synopsis of concept for our multi-use platform
- Elected as the Prescott Campus Point of Contact for the official 2023 ERAU NASA RASC-AL team
- Managed written and verbal communication between the team and ERAU faculty mentors
- Collaborated with the Orbital Mechanics and Scientific and Instrumentation Payloads teams
- Determined the Delta-v for the platform for its trip to the Earth-Moon first Lagrange point (L1) orbit from a 200 kilometer parking orbit above earth
- Selected as a finalist team along with 14 other university teams from around the world
- Participated in the 2023 RASCAL Forum in June and presented to a panel of aerospace industry specialists in front of an audience of around 100 people

projects.title: Project Anubis (Rocket Development Lab)
projects.description:
Worked on creating a two-dimensional axial control module to be placed on future, high altitude rockets developed in the Rocket Development Lab. Focused on Phase 0, a high pressure vessel test, and on Phase 1, a one-dimensional axial control module.
Experience:   
- Reviewed testing procedures for destructive high pressure vessels
- Developed testing procedures for our one dimensional axis balance vehicle with high pressure vessels with separate sections including: test card, assembly verification, testing procedure, anomaly procedures, and shutdown   
- Implemented safety features such as a cover box and anomaly procedures to ensure safety during testing
- Modeled, in SOLIDWORKS, a curved, inflow, pipe adapter as well as structural supports for a 3D printed nozzle
